log.msg: Diagnostic run (Fast 3G, screenshot every 15s, page.jsonl of pending requests at 90s): hasTable was false at 15/30/45/60s and TRUE at 75s and 90s. So the original 'never in 90s, 3/3 runs' was too strong a claim — the real number is borderline, roughly 75-95s with high run-to-run variance, not infinite. The probe's selector and throttle values are correct; this is a real, reproducible-but-noisy slowness.

What is actually pending at the 90s mark: NOT big files. It is about 150 tiny sequential requests — one page.jsonl per ai/ task-folder (the new per-folder listing files this whole task is adding readers for), plus directory.json itself, plus several ext/Panel/*.js and core/Item/Item.js module files still queued. Fast 3G's 562.5ms round-trip latency times a connection-pool limit (browsers cap ~6 concurrent requests per origin) means hundreds of small sequential requests cost far more than the bytes alone would suggest. One pending entry, http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/stream, is a long-lived Server-Sent-Events connection that never finishes by design (it is not blocking anything, it just always shows as pending).

Wi-Fi-like top 5 requests by bytes (of the ~9.6 MB total): 1) http://127.0.0.1:8090/log/prompts?n=400 - 446 KB, 2) framework/ai/board.jsonl - 407 KB, 3) one task's own page.jsonl (2026/09/24/prompt-mechanics-2/chat-as-right-hand-column) - 258 KB, 4) framework/directory.json - 179 KB, 5) a Material Icons webfont (fonts.gstatic.com) - 129 KB.
